newsitem.title: USA: Herman says tentative UPS deal covers many issues.
newsitem.headline: Herman says tentative UPS deal covers many issues.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department Secretary Alexis Herman said on Tuesday the just-formed tentative contract deal between the United Parcel Service and the striking Teamsters union covers multiple issues.

When asked if there was one issue that bridged the gap between the giant parcel carrier and striking union members, Herman said: "There were a multiple number of issues that were certainly part of this agreement. This was obviously a very complicated agreement over many issues and I don't believe there was necessarily any one issue..."
Herman was speaking at a news conference also attended by UPS chief negotiator David Murray, Teamsters President Ron Carey and other key negotiators including Federal mediators.
Murray said that details of the contract, tentatively agreed to earlier on Monday night, would be released at a later date.

"I don't think it would be appropriate to talk about the terms of the agreement at this time. That's going to be communicated to our employees and union officials within the next couple of days," he said.
